messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT detected in prod-west at 2026-03-15T03:44:36Z - elevated tail latency on inference endpoints. Suspected kv-cache growth + continuous-batching interaction. Alert page: @maya (oncall)

maya (oncall): I'm on it. Acknowledge. Looking at dashboards now — p99 is up ~3.2s, error rate creeping from 0.1% -> 1.8% on mixed-request nodes.

kevin: seeing a rapid rise in KV cache size on host pool gw-prod-west-3, evictions dropping to 0. External mem pressure + long requests stacking.

sasha: logs show a lot of long-running reranker requests interleaved with short chat generation. Batching window is growing due to KV cache misses. Could be starvation of short requests.

maya (oncall): tagging infra. @opsbot can you surface the batch-scheduler queue lengths and per-shard mix?

opsbot: batch-scheduler queues: short-req-queue length spiked x12 on nodes [gw-prod-west-2..4]. Long-req-queue holding steady. KV cache hit rate dropped from 87% -> 61% in last 12m. Prefetch tasks backlog increased.

kevin: copying relevant metric snippets:
```
metric: inference.p99_latency (prod-west)
- 03:32 -> 420ms
- 03:40 -> 1.1s
- 03:44 -> 3.2s
kv_cache.size_per_node gw-prod-west-3: 82GB -> 231GB in 18m
kv_cache.evictions/min: 120 -> 8
```

sasha: this looks like a cache blowup combined with continuous-batching growth. If KV cache isn't evicting, batch windows expand due to heavy KV prefetch and long sequences. Short requests starve.

maya (oncall): Immediate mitigations we can try (runbook-ish):
- scale down `batch.window_ms` on prod-west routing for affected model variants
- enable aggressive kv-cache eviction policy on the hostpool
- temporarily pin heavy reranking traffic to dedicated nodes if possible
- if no quick win, roll back latest scheduler config change from 03:10

ryan: I can push a quick batch-window override. Doing a canary to one rack now.

kevin: I'm toggling eviction thresholds on gw-prod-west-3.

sasha: I'll prepare a short-request anti-starvation policy patch for the scheduler to prefer filling short request slots first.

maya (oncall): steps recorded. Start with least-risky: batch-window override -> observe 1 rack -> if p99 drops, roll to others. Keep customer-impact comms ready.

kevin: ran command on rack-2 canary:
```
redwoodctl apply --scope rack:gw-prod-west-2 --set batch.window_ms=5
kubectl annotate nodes gw-prod-west-2 redwood/mitigation=kv-burst-20260315
```
Return: success. Watching.

opsbot: canary metrics at +90s: p99 on rack-2 -> 210ms (was 1.8s). Total errors down. Other racks still high.

maya (oncall): good. Roll to remaining racks in a controlled fashion. kevin, coordinate rollout + throttle.

kevin: rolling to gw-prod-west-1 and gw-prod-west-4 with 30s wait between.

sasha: meanwhile I'm applying a soft patch to the scheduler:
```
# scheduler patch: prefer_short_requests = true (soft)
kubectl patch cm batch-scheduler-config -p '{"data":{"prefer_short_requests":"true"}}'
```
This is a non-disruptive config reload. Will both reduce queue build-up and limit long-request preemption.

opsbot: config applied to scheduler-controller. Observed drop in short-queue length across shards in ~40s.

customer-success: flagging that two enterprise customers (Acme Analytics, LexiSearch) had elevated latency and a handful of timeouts over last 20m. Preparing outreach.

maya (oncall): good note. I'll paste an incident stub for CS: short impact, some timed out requests during 03:28-03:48, mitigation applied, followup to include timeline and RCA.

sasha: small caveat — I'm seeing one worker with huge KV vnodes pinned (gw-prod-west-3). Even with batch-window low, if cache doesn't evict we risk OOM later. kevin — eviction toggle effectiveness?

kevin: eviction toggle kicked in and we saw evictions increase to expected baseline. KV size on node 3 trending down from 231GB -> 156GB in 8m.

maya (oncall): opsbot, please keep monitoring Prefetch backlog and batch windows. If any rack shows p99 > 1s after these changes, we consider routing a percentage of traffic to prod-east as temporary load shedding.

opsbot: ack. Prefetch backlog normalized to pre-incident levels on racks 1,2,4. gw-prod-west-3 still trending down.

deploy-bot: Note: a scheduled patch to batch-scheduler config (version 20260315-03) was deployed at 03:10; curl to /health returned 200. No automatic rollback executed.

maya (oncall): let's record that the config at 03:10 likely reduced fairness in practice under mixed workloads. Need a postmortem item: scheduler change testing coverage for mixed short/long traffic.

kevin: one more protective control: disabled continuous prefetch for high-memory models on prod-west for 30m window.

sasha: that's live. Also added a guard in scheduler to cap max batching window to 50ms for mixed-mode queues.

opsbot: after rollouts, cluster-wide p99 is back down to ~190ms, errors near baseline. Prefetch backlog cleared. KV sizes decreasing.

maya (oncall): excellent. Next: create incident ticket, assign owners for RCA, and handoff. I'll prepare a short incident summary for execs and CS.

maya (oncall): Impact summary draft:
- scope: prod-west inference cluster
- timeframe: ~03:22 -> 03:50 UTC
- impact: spike in p99 latency up to 3.2s, error rate peaked at 1.8%, estimated 4-6% of requests experienced >1s latency, limited number of timeouts (approx 0.03% overall) affecting some enterprise sessions
- immediate remediation: batch.window override, aggressive kv eviction toggles, soft scheduler patch to prefer short requests, temporary prefetch disable for heavy models
- customer comms: CS notified customers; targeted outreach for Acme Analytics, LexiSearch

kevin: recorded incident ticket INC-20260315-042, assigned to sasha (lead on scheduler RCA) and kevin (KV cache investigation).

sasha: accepted. Will run hypothesis tests: 1) scheduler prioritization change effect under synthetic mixed workload, 2) kv eviction policy tuning and long-tail eviction correctness.

maya (oncall): handing off to next oncall: @ryan will cover next 8 hours. I'll be available for questions.

ryan: @maya thanks, taking over. All mitigations stay in place for now; we'll start rolling controlled re-enablement once metrics stable for 60m.

opsbot: monitoring baseline OK. Will page if any regression.

maya (oncall): final note: please include the exact commands and config diffs in the postmortem. I'll attach logs and dashboards link to INC-20260315-042.

customer-success: will draft the customer-safe summary and send to CS thread once final timeline confirmed.

kevin: dropping small diff of the eviction toggle for the record:
```
- kv.eviction_policy = \"lru\"
+ kv.eviction_policy = \"lru_aggressive\"
+ kv.eviction_target = 70GB
```

sasha: and scheduler soft patch diff:
```
+ prefer_short_requests = true
+ max_batch_window_ms = 50
```

maya (oncall): thanks team. Handing final notes to postmortem. Closing hands-on operations for this incident at 04:12 UTC. Marking this thread for postmortem follow-up and RCA assignment.

incident-bot: Incident resolved (mitigations applied) at 2026-03-15T04:12:39Z. Severity: S2. Linked ticket: INC-20260315-042."
